To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

increased norepinephrin (NE) sensitive intracellular Ca(2+) pool (presumably the sarcoplasmic Ca(2+) reticulum, or SR), in the caudai artery of spontaneously hypertenisive rats (SHR), at least in part may account for the enhanced contraction observed in response of NE stimulation in the absence or in the presence of extracellular Ca(2+).

the magnitude of the contractions evoked in the presence of norepinephine and caffeine in Ca 2+-free solution is significantly greater in the caudl artery from spontaneously hypertensive rats than in the caudil artery from normotensive control rats, and the contractions evokved by both agonists in Ca2+-freesolution are mediated primarily through activation of postsynaptice alpha 1-adrenceptors.
the magnitude of contractions evoked from the caudal arteries of SHR in the absence of external Ca2+ is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intracellular Ca2+, particularly that of sarcoplasmic Ca2+, in the development and maintenance of hypertension.
elucidating the mechanism by which increased intracellular Ca2+, in response to NE stimulation, may be involved in the pathophysiology of hypertension in SHR.
the role of the intracellular Ca2+, specifically that stored in the SR, in the development of vascular smooth muscle contractility in SHR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in intracellular calcium pool in SHR is a result of the increased sensitivity of the alpha 1-adrenergic receptor to NE.
the increased Ca2+ pool is a result of an increased number of SR Ca2+ pump sites, which is a direct consequence of the increased Ca2+-ATPase activity in SHR.
the increased intracellular Ca2+-pool in SHR caudals is not the cause of hypertension but is a result of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intracellular Ca2+-sensitive mechanisms are increased in SHR cauda arteries.
the increased intracellular Ca2+-pool in SHR is due to the increased expression of SR Ca2+-ATPase and SERCA2a protein in SHR.

the intracellular Ca2+-pool is increased in SHR arteries, and the increased intracellular Ca2+, in conjunction with the increased alpha 1-adrenergic responsiveness in SHR arteries, may contribute to the increased contractility observed in these vessels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SR Ca2+ pool is increased in SHR arteries.
the increased intracellular Ca2+-store in SHR is not a consequence of hypertension, but rather it is a pre-hypertensive event.

the increased contraction in response to NE in Ca2+ free solution in SHR cauda arteries is due to the increased sensitivity of alpha1 receptors and the increased intracellular Ca2+, presumably from sarcoplasmic Ca2+ pool.
